Diagnose Selection Conditioning Sensitivity

Source: R/selection-sensitivity-diagnostics.R
selection_sensitivity_diagnostics.Rd

Describes how integrating the contexts retained by a fitted selection model would reweight their pre-selection Gaussian distribution. This compares reporting models; it is not a numerical approximation error bound.

Usage

selection_sensitivity_diagnostics(
  object,
  max_posterior_samples = 256L,
  latent_samples = 512L,
  seed = 1L,
  integration_control = NULL
)

add_selection_sensitivity_diagnostics(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted normal-outcome model with a bound selection model.

max_posterior_samples

Maximum number of posterior draws to evaluate. A positive integer of at least 10, or Inf for all posterior draws. Draws are deterministically thinned over posterior row order.

latent_samples

Number of fresh pre-selection retained-context draws per posterior draw. Must be one finite integer of at least 2; defaults to 512.

seed

Integer seed for the diagnostic simulation. The calling R session's random-number state is restored before returning.

integration_control

Optional settings from set_selection_likelihood_control() for diagnostic event integration. NULL uses the fitted model's settings.

...

Simulation arguments passed to selection_sensitivity_diagnostics().

Value

A data frame with one row per connected source unit, identified by block, comma-separated observation rows, and n_estimates. The ess_fraction, total_variation, and log_weight_iqr summaries each have _q05, _median, and _q95 columns across all evaluated posterior draws, including non-selection draws. The ess_fraction_mcse and total_variation_mcse columns have _median and _max suffixes for conditional Monte Carlo uncertainty. integration_relative_mcse_max and integration_relative_quadrature_error_max are maxima over constituent event evaluations, not an error bound for the multiplied unit weight. posterior_samples, total_posterior_samples, and latent_samples report the simulation budgets. The settings attribute records max_posterior_samples, latent_samples, seed, and integration_control. The target attribute records the comparison, fitted and reference models, applicability, source roles, fitted and reference sampling structures, publication groups, likelihood unit, row blocks, and resolved event integration settings. The add function returns the fitted object.

Details

At each posterior draw the fitted model defines a conditional Gaussian response law, retained contexts, and any best-rule publication groups. The diagnostic evaluates each Gaussian selection unit's normalizer at fresh retained contexts, preserving the fitted product or best weight rule and any best-rule publication groups. Product-only models require no grouping. Within a connected source unit, their product gives the relative reweighting when the retained contexts are integrated before selection normalization. Sampling-conditioned comparisons use the fitted candidate factors, including singular declared support. Integration diagnostics report maxima over the constituent event evaluations, rather than an error bound for their product.

ess_fraction estimates mean(W)^2 / mean(W^2); this is a retained-context reweighting ESS fraction within each posterior parameter state, not the posterior sample ESS. total_variation estimates the distance between the pre-selection context law and its normalized W-reweighted law. The fitted and reference conditioning specifications, publication identities, and source roles are retained in the target attribute. With no retained context this comparison is inapplicable and its reweighting is identically constant.

The fitted weight rule is held fixed. These summaries do not compare arbitrary weight rules, identify the correct reporting mechanism, or reveal parameter regions absent from the fitted posterior.

Simulation budgets control diagnostic Monte Carlo precision separately from the fitted Gaussian event integration controls. The largest unit-level posterior-median total variation distance is silent up to 0.05, produces a message above 0.05 and below 0.10, and a warning from 0.10. These notifications describe sensitivity rather than statistical adequacy.

This optional comparison is computed only when requested; fitting does not compute it. Calls without simulation arguments reuse an explicitly stored result, and explicit settings reuse it only when they match. Use add_selection_sensitivity_diagnostics() to compute and store a result. Chain extension silently refreshes only stored diagnostics using their stored simulation settings; label-only updates retain them. Failed refreshes remain stored as unavailable without discarding the fitted posterior. Call selection_sensitivity_diagnostics() to inspect the comparison or its error. Sensitivity notifications are emitted only by these explicit helper calls, not by fitting, extension, or ordinary model printing.

The substantial-sensitivity warning has class RoBMA_selection_sensitivity_warning, retaining simpleWarning, warning, and condition. Its fields are maximum_total_variation, threshold (0.10), and comparison ("retained_context_reweighting"). Own nonfinite normalizer refusals have class RoBMA_selection_sensitivity_normalizer_unavailable and fields reason, posterior_draw (the evaluated posterior-row index), latent_draw, event, and the observed log_mass values. Unsupported retained covariance has class RoBMA_selection_sensitivity_covariance_unavailable and reason = "retained_covariance_unavailable". Both refusals inherit from RoBMA_selection_sensitivity_error, simpleError, error, and condition. Downstream integration failures retain their original conditions.
